title: Madeira at New Year: fireworks, weather and tips
author: Brogan
intro: Madeira's New Year's Eve fireworks over Funchal are among the most famous in the world, watched from the seafront, the hills and dozens of cruise ships in the bay. It's also mild, at about 20°C by day. Here's what to expect, where to watch and how to plan the trip.
seo_title: Madeira at New Year 2026: fireworks, weather and tips
seo_description: Funchal's New Year fireworks light up the whole bay, with cruise ships offshore and highs of about 20°C. Where to watch, when to book and what else is on.

sections.heading: The short answer
sections.text:
- **Fireworks:** midnight, 31 December
- **Where:** all around Funchal bay
- **Daytime highs:** about 20°C
- **Christmas lights:** from 1 December
- **Book:** as early as you can

We checked these details in November 2026. The 2026/27 programme hadn't been fully published, so confirm times and events nearer the date.

sections.heading: The fireworks
sections.text:
At midnight, fireworks go up from dozens of launch sites around Funchal's amphitheatre-shaped bay, so the whole city seems to light up at once. The display once held a Guinness World Record as the largest fireworks show in the world.

It's a short, intense show. To welcome 2026, the display lasted about eight minutes, and 11 cruise ships were anchored in the bay, sounding their horns at midnight. More than 30,000 people watched from the port area alone.

Local knowledge: the weather can spoil the view. Low cloud and light rain affected the 2025/26 show in parts of the city, so a spot lower down near the seafront is the safest bet.

sections.heading: Where to watch
sections.text:
- **The seafront and marina:** the busiest and most atmospheric spot, with music and stalls. Arrive by about 10pm to get a place.
- **A hotel balcony or terrace:** many Funchal hotels face the bay and hold New Year parties. Rooms with a sea view sell out first.
- **The hills above Funchal:** quieter, with the whole display spread out below you, but you'll need transport back.
- **From a boat:** catamaran trips go out into the bay. Book well ahead, and check what happens if the sea is rough.

Roads into central Funchal get very busy on the night, and some close, so plan how you'll get back to your hotel.

sections.heading: Weather in December and January
sections.text: Madeira is mild rather than hot in winter, with highs of about 20°C in December and 19°C in January. Evenings are cooler, and the mountains are much colder than the coast. Rain is more likely than in summer, especially in the north of the island. It's good weather for walking, the botanical gardens and the levada trails, and warm enough for lunch outside on a sunny day. Our [Madeira or Tenerife](/blog/madeira-or-tenerife) guide compares it with the Canaries if you want more beach weather.

sections.heading: Christmas and the festive season
sections.text:
New Year is the finale of a festive season that runs through December and into January:

- **Christmas lights:** switched on across central Funchal from 1 December 2026, and listed in the official calendar until the second week of January.
- **Market Night (23 December):** traditionally the Mercado dos Lavradores and the streets around it stay open late, with food, music and crowds. Check this year's programme.
- **New Year's Day:** a quiet day, with many shops closed, so plan a walk rather than shopping.

Tip: if you'd like the lights without the New Year prices, go in the first half of December or the first week of January. The lights are still on and hotels are much cheaper.

sections.heading: What else to do that week
sections.text:
- **Monte:** take the cable car up from the seafront, see the gardens and ride the traditional wicker toboggans back down part of the way.
- **A levada walk:** the island's irrigation channels make easy, mostly flat walks through forest and along hillsides. Go with a guide if the weather is unsettled.
- **Pico do Arieiro:** the drive up for sunrise above the clouds is spectacular, but it can be near freezing at the top in winter.
- **Funchal old town:** the painted doors of Rua de Santa Maria, and plenty of places for a poncha, the local rum drink.

sections.heading: Booking and getting there
sections.text:
There are direct flights to Madeira from many UK airports, taking about four hours from London. New Year is the island's busiest week, so flights and hotels cost the most and sell out early. Many people book a year ahead.

The landing at Madeira is famous for its strong winds, and flights are sometimes diverted. Our guide to [which side of the plane to sit on flying to Madeira](/blog/which-side-of-the-plane-to-sit-on-flying-to-madeira) covers the approach. For more New Year ideas, see the [New Year holidays](/destinations/new-year-holidays) page or [Hogmanay in Edinburgh](/blog/hogmanay-in-edinburgh-2026), and if you can't decide, add a few to somewhere.party and let the draw choose.

faqs.question: What time are the Madeira New Year fireworks?
faqs.answer: At midnight on 31 December. The display usually lasts around eight minutes and is launched from many sites around Funchal bay.

faqs.question: Is Madeira warm at New Year?
faqs.answer: Mild rather than hot. Daytime highs are about 20°C in December and 19°C in January, with cooler evenings and colder mountains.

faqs.question: Where is the best place to watch the Madeira fireworks?
faqs.answer: The Funchal seafront is the busiest spot. A hotel with a bay view, the hills above the city or a boat trip give a different view. Book early.

faqs.question: When should I book Madeira for New Year?
faqs.answer: As early as you can. New Year is the island's busiest week, and many people book a year ahead.
